subject: Next steps: FinApps stakeholder map, vendor onboarding path, and PO timeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Hart <megan.hart@finapps.com>, Tom Riley <tom.riley@finapps.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & quick recap from today — stakeholder map + procurement path

Hi Megan / Tom —

Thanks for a constructive call earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum with procurement and legal at FinApps.

What I heard (summary):
- Primary use case: low-latency inference for payment reconciliation and fraud alerts (batch + realtime mix).
- Target launch: pilot with 3 internal apps in Q4; pilot budget owned by Payments team.
- Key stakeholders:
  * Economic buyer: Megan Hart (Payments VP) — owns budget + ROI signoff.
  * Technical lead: Tom Riley — will validate integration and SLOs.
  * Security reviewer: InfoSec (procurement will route to security for SOC2 evidence).
  * Procurement contact: procurement@finapps.com (you mentioned they prefer a single PDF SOW + pricing and a PO template).

Immediate asks / next steps (recommended):
1) I’ll send a one-page SOW + pricing summary and a procurement Qs doc for your team to circulate to procurement/security (attached).
2) Can you confirm the procurement workflow: who signs, who raises PO, and estimated time to issue PO once SOW is accepted?
3) Please share any specific vendor-onboarding forms or FedRAMP/SOC2 evidence repository links — we’ll attach those to the procurement packet.

Proposed timeline:
- Jul 13: Send SOW + procurement Qs (we’ll do this today).
- Jul 16: Align on procurement owner and PO timing.
- Jul 23: Target procurement approval window (you indicated end of July looks feasible).

Attachments I’ll send in the follow-up: Redwood-SOW-FinApps-v1.pdf, redwood-pricing-summary.csv, procurement-questions-finapps.docx

If any of the stakeholder bullets are off, call them out and I’ll update the one-pager before we hand it to procurement.

Thanks again,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

From: Megan Hart <megan.hart@finapps.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Riley <tom.riley@finapps.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 16:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up & quick recap from today — stakeholder map + procurement path

Soojin —

Thanks for the concise summary, that’s accurate. A few clarifications:

- Procurement contact is actually a shared inbox (procurement@finapps.com). Once we have an SOW + pricing they will route to our legal and InfoSec reviewers.
- Legal will generally redline the SOW; our standard play is for vendor to send a final SOW + standard terms.
- PO creation: our procurement ops team raises the PO after budget sign-off (I will own the budget sign-off).
- Timeline: if we get the SOW this week, legal + procurement usually take 7–10 business days. If InfoSec needs additional evidence it can add another 3–5 business days.

Tom: can you confirm technical acceptance criteria we should include in the SOW (throughput, 95th latency target, data handling assurances)?

Appreciate you sharing the procurement Qs doc — I’ll loop procurement once we have it.

Best,
Megan

Megan Hart
VP, Payments | FinApps
megan.hart@finapps.com | (617) 555-9876

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Hart <megan.hart@finapps.com>, Tom Riley <tom.riley@finapps.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@finapps.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: SOW + procurement packet (attached) — action items + ask

Hi all —

Attached is the initial SOW (PDF), a condensed pricing CSV, and a short procurement Qs doc that lists the common evidence items procurement asks for. Highlights:

- Pilot scope: 3 apps, 200k tokens/day expected, can scale to 1M/day in production.
- SLA targets: 95th latency <= 250ms for realtime endpoints; throughput targets listed in the SOW appendix.
- Data handling: no persistent customer PII is stored by default; KV cache controls and encryption-at-rest details are in the appendix.
- Pricing: pilot discounted rate (see pricing CSV). Post-pilot list pricing and options for Dedicated/Private are outlined.

Action items for FinApps:
- Confirm procurement owner who will raise the PO (Megan, you said you’d own budget sign-off; who on procurement ops creates the PO?).
- Confirm whether we should route SOC2 Type II report or a custom security questionnaire first. Procurement said either is fine; InfoSec prefers having SOC2 + the short questionnaire filled out.
- Share any vendor onboarding forms or the PO template if you want SOW formatted to fit your PO fields.

If helpful, we can also prepare a redline-friendly SOW (track changes) to speed legal review.

Next steps (proposed):
1) FinApps confirms procurement ops contact and PO timing.
2) Redwood provides a track-changes SOW if requested.
3) We schedule a 30-min call with InfoSec (if they want to meet) the week of Jul 20.

Attachments:
- Redwood-SOW-FinApps-v1.pdf (2 pages + appendix)
- redwood-pricing-summary.csv
- procurement-questions-finapps.docx

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Cc: Megan Hart <megan.hart@finapps.com>, procurement@finapps.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick note on commercial levers and negotiation guardrails for FinApps deal

Sergio / Laura — quick internal note (also CC’d Megan/procurement for transparency):

Recap: FinApps is primed to pilot in Q4; budget owner is Megan. Procurement window ~7–10 business days after SOW arrives; InfoSec could add 3–5 days.

Commercial asks for us to consider before legal conversation:
- Pilot discount: we offered a pilot discount in the pricing CSV. At renewal we should move to list or discuss Dedicated pricing.
- Revenue recognition: anticipate they will ask for standard PoS terms — payment on net 30 after invoice; procurement sometimes requests a PO before work starts.
- Credits/credits policy: if legal pushes on SLA credits, prefer to limit to a defined cap (2% monthly) for pilot stage.

Can you review the SOW and pricing attached and call out any items we should preemptively adjust before legal sees it? I’d like to keep the SOW redline-friendly and minimize back-and-forth.

Thanks — I’ll update HubSpot with the timeline and attach the documents.

--
Soojin
